title: Swahili Spiced Tea
community: Zanzibar and the Swahili coast — the spiced morning ritual
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Chai ya Viungo — strong black tea brewed with fresh ginger, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon, sweetened and enriched with milk. The Swahili coast's most beloved morning beverage — more spiced than chai masala, more fragrant than plain tea.
longDesc: Swahili spiced tea is the morning ritual of the Tanzanian coast — the tea brewed in a pot with fresh ginger and whole spices, sweetened generously, and served with mahamri or vitumbua. It is the beverage that accompanies the first prayer call and the first light on the Indian Ocean.
ingredients: 3 tbsp black tea leaves (or 4 tea bags)
steps: Combine water with ginger, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon.
Bring to a boil. Simmer 3 minutes to extract spices.
Bring back to a near-boil. Remove just before it boils over.
chefTips: Bring to just before boiling — do not boil after adding milk.
Fresh ginger crushed (not sliced) releases more aromatics.
More sugar than you think — coastal chai is sweet.
cookingScience: See TZA020 for chai brewing science.
sustainabilityTips: Tanzanian tea from Ruvuma and Kagera highlands — some of Africa's finest.
culturalNote: Swahili spiced tea is the beverage of the coast's mornings — the ritual that marks the beginning of every day in Zanzibar, shared at every household table and at every outdoor stall as the island wakes.
